subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Pressure: Force Spread Over Area
description: A 60-second lesson on Pressure: Force Spread Over Area.

hook.text: Stand on a nail and it hurts. Lie on a bed of nails and it doesn't.

buildup.text: Pressure is force divided by area. Smaller area means higher pressure.

discovery.text: In a fluid, pressure pushes equally in every direction at any point.

twist.text: That's why a dam is thicker at the bottom — pressure rises with depth.

climax.text: Hydraulic systems exploit pressure to multiply force over long distances.

punchline.text: Pressure is force with focus — and focus changes everything.

quiz.question: Why is a dam thicker at the bottom than at the top?
options: Water pressure increases with depth, pushing harder on lower walls
The bottom supports the weight of the dam itself
Waves hit the bottom of the dam harder
